title: San Leonardo Half Marathon 2026 Review: What the Race Was Like
seo_title: San Leonardo Half Marathon Review: 2026 Results, Weather, Cut-offs
meta_description: San Leonardo Half Marathon 2026 review: a 4.30am start in Nueva Ecija, 23°C and 89% humidity, a four-hour limit that every finisher made, and 208 half-marathon finishers with a 2:25 median.
dek: What the town half marathon in San Leonardo, Nueva Ecija, was like on 25 October 2026: the start, the weather, the cut-offs, what the entry included and how fast a small field ran.
verdict: Enter if you want a small-town half marathon with a generous four-hour limit and a party at the finish. The 2026 race started at 4.30am from the municipal gym in about 23°C air at 89% humidity, and every one of its 208 half-marathon finishers made the limit, the slowest in 3:42. Half the field finished inside 2:25. The organiser published no route map or aid plan, so expect a local club race rather than a big-city one.

sections.heading: The Race
paragraphs: The San Leonardo Half Marathon is organised by the San Leonardo Runners club and billed as One Big Party Run [1][2]. The 2026 race was based at the San Leonardo Municipal Gym in Nueva Ecija, with a 21 km, a 10 km and a 5 km [1][2]. No route map or course description was published; the rules refer only to a designated route and disqualify runners who cut it short or leave it [1].
Half marathoners assembled at 3.30am for a 4.30am gun; the 10 km started at 5am and the 5 km at 5.30am [1][3].

sections.heading: The Weather: Mild Before Sunrise
paragraphs: Open-Meteo's reanalysis for the grid point at San Leonardo shows about 23°C, a dew point of 21°C to 22°C and 89% to 94% humidity from 4am to 6am, with a light breeze and a clear sky [4]. It warmed to 25°C at 7am, 27°C at 8am and 29°C at 9am [4].
A median half marathoner, at 2:25, finished just before 7am, at about 25°C. The last finishers, past 8am, ran into sunshine at 27°C and more.

sections.heading: Cut-offs and Aid
paragraphs: The limits were four hours for the 21 km, two and a half hours for the 10 km and an hour and a half for the 5 km, and the organiser said they would be strictly enforced [1][3]. They were generous for this field: the slowest of the 208 half-marathon finishers ran 3:42:01, and only three of 397 10 km times are past two and a half hours [5].
The organiser did not publish where drinks stations would be, and advised runners to stay hydrated [1]. Food and drinks after the finish were included for every distance [2].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The half marathon was won in 1:25:16 by a man and 1:37:24 by a woman; tenth place was 1:43:03 [5]. The median finisher took 2:25:28 and the slowest tenth more than 3:08. Sixteen per cent broke two hours and 57% broke 2:30 [5]. Women were few: about 15% of finishers whose gender is listed [5].

The 10 km was the larger race, with 397 finishers. It was won in 38:24 and 53:08, with tenth place at 48:33, a median of 1:24:58 and 12% under an hour [5]. Awards went to the top man and woman and to the three biggest club delegations [1].

sections.heading: Entry and What You Got
paragraphs: The 21 km cost PHP 1,500 early and PHP 1,650 regular, the 10 km PHP 1,200 and 1,300 and the 5 km PHP 850 and 950, plus a PHP 57 fee online [1][2]. Half marathoners got a singlet, sun visor, chip-timed bib, finisher shirt and medal; 10 km runners the same without the visor; 5 km runners a singlet, bib and medal [2]. Entries could not be refunded or transferred, and kits not claimed before the race were not released afterwards [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the Next Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a low-key provincial half marathon with a four-hour limit that nobody missed in 2026, mild pre-dawn air and food at the finish. A sub-two-hour runner finishes in the top sixth.
Think twice if you want a known, measured course, published aid stations or a big field.
A 2027 date had not been announced when this was written.
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's entry page and posters, the full results and modelled weather data.

faqs.question: How fast is the San Leonardo Half Marathon field?
faqs.answer: Relaxed. In 2026, 208 runners finished the 21 km with a median of 2:25:28; 16% broke two hours and the slowest tenth took more than 3:08. It was won in 1:25:16 by a man and 1:37:24 by a woman, and tenth place was 1:43:03.

faqs.question: Does anyone miss the San Leonardo Half Marathon cut-off?
faqs.answer: Almost nobody. The 2026 limit was four hours for the 21 km, and the slowest of 208 finishers ran 3:42:01. In the 10 km, with a two-and-a-half-hour limit, only three of 397 finishers were slower. The organiser said the limits would be strictly enforced.

faqs.question: What is the weather like at the San Leonardo Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Mild before sunrise. Modelled weather for San Leonardo shows about 23°C and 89% to 94% humidity from 4am to 6am on race day in 2026, under a clear sky. It reached 25°C at 7am and 27°C at 8am, so most half marathoners finished before the heat.

editorial_notes: Written 2026-11-06 about the edition that ran on Sunday 25 October 2026; whether it was the first edition, and the next edition's date, were not found. Evidence beyond the organiser's entry page and the results is thin: no route map, aid plan, news report or runner account was found, and the organiser's Facebook page could not be read. The venue is from the organiser's poster. Finish-time figures are Run SEA's analysis of the official Outdoor Statement results (gun or chip not stated); gender is blank for 10 half-marathon and 9 10 km finishers, so the share of women is of those listed. Weather is Open-Meteo modelled reanalysis for the grid point at San Leonardo, not a station observation. No rating.
